subtitle.title: Why large numbers matter
subtitle.content: Large numbers describe populations, distances, money, data and quantities too large to count individually. Place-value notation makes them readable, comparable and useful for estimation.

left.heading: Indian system
left.content: Group the last three digits, then groups of two: 12,34,56,789.

right.heading: International system
right.content: Group digits in threes from the right: 123,456,789.

subtitle.title: Face value and place value
subtitle.content: Face value is the digit itself. Place value depends on position. In 5,42,318, the digit 4 has face value 4 and place value 40,000.

subtitle.title: Expanded form
facts: A zero is a placeholder; do not drop an empty place.

subtitle.title: Read and write large numbers
steps: Group digits using the chosen place-value system.
Place commas at the correct boundaries.
Read each group with its period name.
Write zero placeholders wherever a place has no value.
Check that the written number has the same digits as the original.

subtitle.title: Compare large numbers
subtitle.content: First compare the number of digits. If the counts match, compare from the leftmost digit until the first difference. The larger digit at that position decides the greater number.

subtitle.title: Round to a chosen place
steps: Identify the place to which you are rounding.
Look at the digit immediately to its right.
If that digit is 0–4, keep the rounding digit unchanged; if it is 5–9, increase it by one.
Replace all digits to the right with zeroes.
Check that the rounded number is close to the original.

subtitle.title: Place-value check
subtitle.question: In 7,35,42,816, what is the place value of 5?
subtitle.answer: 5,00,000; the 5 is in the lakhs place.

subtitle.title: Number-name check
subtitle.question: Write 4,08,05,019 in words using the Indian system.
subtitle.answer: Four crore eight lakh five thousand nineteen.

subtitle.title: Estimation check
subtitle.question: Round 8,76,549 to the nearest ten thousand.
subtitle.answer: 8,80,000; the thousands digit is 6, so the ten-thousands digit increases from 7 to 8.

subtitle.title: Expression or equation?
subtitle.content: An arithmetic expression combines numbers and operation signs, such as 24 + 6 × 3. An equation states that two expressions are equal and includes an equals sign.

subtitle.title: Four basic operations
facts: Combines quantities; result is the sum.
Finds a difference or what remains.
Equal sharing or finding the number of groups.

subtitle.title: Order of operations
subtitle.content: Evaluate grouping symbols first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Multiplication does not automatically come before division; they share priority.

subtitle.title: Evaluate a bracketed expression
steps: Work inside the innermost brackets first.
Complete multiplication and division from left to right.
Complete addition and subtraction from left to right.
Show intermediate steps so the order is clear.
Check the result using an estimate or inverse operation.

subtitle.title: Mental calculation strategies
subtitle.content: Make tens or hundreds, split a number into convenient parts, use known multiplication facts and apply operation properties when they preserve the value.

subtitle.title: Common order-of-operations mistake
subtitle.content: Do not calculate strictly left to right when operations have different priority. Multiplication and division have equal priority; addition and subtraction have equal priority.

subtitle.title: Order check
subtitle.question: Evaluate 18 − 6 ÷ 3.

subtitle.title: Bracket check
subtitle.question: Evaluate (18 − 6) ÷ 3.

subtitle.title: Distributive property check
subtitle.question: Calculate 7 × 19 using a convenient split.

subtitle.title: Expression check
subtitle.question: Evaluate 15 + 9 × 2.

subtitle.title: Meaning of the decimal point
subtitle.content: The decimal point separates the whole-number part from the fractional part. To its right are tenths, hundredths, thousandths and smaller place values.

subtitle.title: Decimals as fractions
subtitle.content: A decimal can represent a fraction with denominator 10, 100, 1000 and so on. For example, 0.37 means 37 hundredths, or 37/100.

subtitle.title: Read a decimal
steps: Read the whole-number part first.
Identify the place value of the final digit after the decimal point.
Use tenths, hundredths or thousandths to state the fractional part precisely.
Do not confuse 0.5 with 0.05; the zero changes the place value.

subtitle.title: Add or subtract decimals
steps: Write numbers one below the other with decimal points aligned.
Add zeroes at the end if needed, for example 2.5 = 2.50.
Add or subtract as with whole numbers.
Place the decimal point directly below the other decimal points.
Check the answer with an estimate.

subtitle.title: Decimals in daily life
subtitle.content: Decimals are used for money, length, mass, capacity and measurements. Always check the unit and required precision before calculating.

subtitle.title: Do not compare by digit count
subtitle.content: A decimal with more digits is not automatically greater. Compare place values: 0.8 = 0.80, which is greater than 0.75.

subtitle.title: Place-value check
subtitle.question: What is the value of 6 in 4.263?

subtitle.title: Comparison check
subtitle.question: Which is greater: 0.7 or 0.65?

subtitle.title: Addition check
subtitle.question: Calculate 3.45 + 1.8.

subtitle.title: Letters represent numbers
subtitle.content: A letter used in mathematics can stand for an unknown or changing number. It is called a variable. For example, n can represent the number of objects in a group.

subtitle.title: Parts of an algebraic expression
facts: A letter representing a number, such as x.
The number multiplying a variable; in 5a it is 5.
A part separated by plus or minus signs.
A combination of numbers, variables and operations.

subtitle.title: Translate words into expressions
subtitle.content: 'Five more than n' is n + 5; 'five times n' is 5n; 'n decreased by five' is n − 5. The order of words changes the operation and sometimes the order.

left.heading: 3x
left.content: Three times x. If x = 4, the value is 12.

right.heading: x + 3
right.content: Three more than x. If x = 4, the value is 7.

subtitle.title: Evaluate by substitution
steps: Write the value given for each variable.
Replace every occurrence of the variable with that value.
Use brackets when substituting a negative number.
Follow the order of operations and simplify.
Check by substituting the value again.

subtitle.title: Expressions describe patterns
subtitle.content: A rule such as 'add 4 each time' can be described with a variable. If the starting number is n, the next number is n + 4.

subtitle.title: Multiplication notation
facts: Written as x² when square notation is introduced.

subtitle.title: Equality means balance
subtitle.content: An equation says that two expressions have the same value. The equals sign means 'is equal to'; it does not simply mean 'write the answer next'.

subtitle.title: Do not confuse 2x and x²
subtitle.content: 2x means 2 multiplied by x. x² means x multiplied by itself. If x = 3, then 2x = 6 but x² = 9.

subtitle.title: Translate a phrase
subtitle.question: Write '7 more than p' as an expression.

subtitle.title: Identify parts
subtitle.question: In 8m + 3, identify the variable, coefficient and constant.

subtitle.title: Substitution check
subtitle.question: Find 4a − 1 when a = 5.

subtitle.title: Point, line, segment and ray
subtitle.content: A point marks an exact position. A line extends endlessly in both directions. A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint and continues endlessly in one direction.

subtitle.title: Line relationships
facts: Lines in the same plane that never meet.
Lines that cross at a common point.
A line that crosses two or more lines.

left.heading: Parallel
left.content: The perpendicular distance between the lines remains constant; they do not meet.

right.heading: Intersecting
right.content: The lines meet at one point. If they meet at 90°, they are perpendicular.

subtitle.title: How an angle is formed
subtitle.content: An angle is formed by two rays with a common endpoint. The common endpoint is the vertex and the rays are the arms of the angle.

subtitle.title: Measure an angle with a protractor
steps: Place the protractor's centre mark exactly on the vertex.
Align its baseline with one arm of the angle.
Read the scale that starts at 0° on that arm.
Check whether the result matches the angle's apparent size.
Write the degree symbol with the measurement.

subtitle.title: Estimate before measuring
subtitle.content: First decide whether an angle is acute, right, obtuse or straight. Estimation helps detect a wrong protractor scale or incorrect alignment.

subtitle.title: Drawing lines correctly
subtitle.content: A line segment has two endpoints; a line has no endpoints. Use arrowheads at both ends of a drawn line to show that it continues.

subtitle.title: Line relationship check
subtitle.question: What is the difference between perpendicular and parallel lines?
subtitle.answer: Perpendicular lines intersect at 90°; parallel lines in the same plane never intersect.

subtitle.title: Angle type check
subtitle.question: An angle measures 125°. What type is it?
subtitle.answer: Obtuse, because it is greater than 90° and less than 180°.

subtitle.title: Ray check
subtitle.question: How many endpoints does a ray have?
subtitle.answer: One endpoint. It extends endlessly in one direction.

subtitle.title: Protractor check
subtitle.question: Where should the centre mark of a protractor be placed?
subtitle.answer: Exactly on the vertex of the angle.

chapters.chapterLabel: Divisibility · factors · multiples · prime numbers · patterns
chapters.title: Number Play

subtitle.title: Look for number structure
subtitle.content: Number puzzles become easier when we examine place value, odd and even numbers, factors, multiples, remainders and repeating patterns instead of guessing.

subtitle.title: Divisibility tests
facts: Sum of digits is divisible by 3.
Sum of digits is divisible by 9.

subtitle.title: Factors and multiples
subtitle.content: A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is obtained by multiplying a number by a whole number. For example, 4 is a factor of 20; 20 and 24 are multiples of 4.

left.heading: Prime
left.content: A whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself. Example: 13.

right.heading: Composite
right.content: A whole number greater than 1 with more than two factors. Example: 12.

subtitle.title: Test divisibility by 3
steps: Add all the digits of the number.
Check whether the digit sum is divisible by 3.
If it is, the original number is divisible by 3.
Example: 4,326 has digit sum 15, so it is divisible by 3.

subtitle.title: Number patterns
subtitle.content: A sequence follows a rule. The rule may add, subtract, multiply, alternate operations or use a relationship between shapes and numbers.

subtitle.title: Remainders
subtitle.content: The remainder is what is left after making as many equal groups as possible. It is always smaller than the divisor.

subtitle.title: Factor is not the same as multiple
subtitle.content: A factor divides a number; a multiple is produced by multiplying. Five is a factor of 20, while 20, 25 and 30 are multiples of 5.

subtitle.title: Divisibility check
subtitle.question: Is 7,452 divisible by 3?
subtitle.answer: Yes. Its digit sum is 7 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 18, which is divisible by 3.

subtitle.title: Prime number check
subtitle.question: Why is 2 the only even prime number?
subtitle.answer: Every other even number is divisible by 2 and has at least three factors: 1, 2 and itself.

subtitle.title: Factor check
subtitle.question: List all positive factors of 18.

chapters.title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

subtitle.title: Three lines can form a triangle
subtitle.content: When three non-parallel lines intersect pairwise at three distinct points, they can enclose a triangular region. The intersection points are its vertices.

subtitle.title: Parts of a triangle
facts: The three line segments forming its boundary.
The sum of the lengths of all three sides.

left.heading: Equilateral
left.content: All three sides are equal; each interior angle is 60°.

right.heading: Isosceles
right.content: At least two sides are equal; angles opposite equal sides are equal.

subtitle.title: Classify triangles by angles
facts: All three angles are less than 90°.

subtitle.title: Angle sum of a triangle
subtitle.content: The three interior angles of every triangle add up to 180°. If two angles are known, subtract their sum from 180° to find the third.

subtitle.title: Find an unknown triangle angle
steps: Write the two known interior angles.
Add the known angles.
Subtract their sum from 180°.
Check that all three angles total 180°.

subtitle.title: Vertically opposite angles
subtitle.content: When two straight lines intersect, vertically opposite angles are equal. Adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

subtitle.title: Triangle inequality
subtitle.facts: The sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side.

subtitle.title: Not every three lengths form a triangle
subtitle.content: Lengths 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm cannot form a triangle because 2 + 3 is not greater than 6.

subtitle.title: Angle-sum check
subtitle.question: A triangle has angles 45° and 65°. Find the third angle.

subtitle.title: Classify by sides
subtitle.question: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. Classify it by sides.
subtitle.answer: Isosceles, because two sides are equal.

subtitle.title: Vertically opposite angles
subtitle.question: What is the relationship between vertically opposite angles?

chapters.chapterLabel: Parts of a whole · equivalence · comparison · operations
chapters.title: Working with Fractions

subtitle.title: Meaning of a fraction
subtitle.content: A fraction represents equal parts of a whole or collection. In a/b, a is the numerator and b is the denominator; the denominator cannot be zero.

subtitle.title: Types of fractions
facts: Numerator is smaller than denominator, e.g. 3/5.
Numerator is equal to or greater than denominator, e.g. 7/4.
A whole number and a proper fraction, e.g. 1 3/4.

subtitle.title: Equivalent fractions
subtitle.content: Fractions are equivalent when they represent the same quantity. Multiply or divide both numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number to make an equivalent fraction.

subtitle.title: Simplify a fraction
steps: Find a common factor of the numerator and denominator.
Divide both by the same factor.
Repeat until no common factor greater than 1 remains.
Check that the value has not changed.

left.heading: Like fractions
left.content: Same denominator, such as 2/7 and 5/7. Compare numerators directly.

right.heading: Unlike fractions
right.content: Different denominators, such as 1/3 and 2/5. Use equivalent fractions or a common denominator.

subtitle.title: Compare fractions with the same denominator
subtitle.content: When denominators are equal, compare numerators. The larger numerator represents more equal-sized parts of the same whole.

subtitle.title: Add fractions with unlike denominators
steps: Find a common denominator.
Rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction.
Add the numerators and keep the common denominator.
Simplify the answer if possible.

subtitle.title: Fractions on a number line
subtitle.content: Divide each unit interval into as many equal parts as the denominator. Count the numerator's parts from zero to locate the fraction.

subtitle.title: Fraction of a quantity
facts: Divide the quantity by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.
The result should be sensible compared with the original quantity.

subtitle.title: Do not add denominators
subtitle.content: For same-denominator fractions, 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4, not 3/8. The denominator describes the size of each part.

subtitle.title: Equivalent fraction check
subtitle.question: Write an equivalent fraction for 3/5 with denominator 20.

subtitle.title: Simplify check
subtitle.question: Simplify 18/24.

subtitle.title: Addition check
subtitle.question: Calculate 2/7 + 3/7.

subtitle.title: Fraction of a quantity
subtitle.question: Find 2/3 of 18.
subtitle.answer: 12. Divide 18 by 3 to get 6, then multiply by 2.

chapters.title: Locating Places on the Earth
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A globe is a model of Earth; maps show all or part of its surface. Directions, symbols, scale, latitudes and longitudes help us locate places accurately.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Latitude measures distance north or south of the Equator; longitude measures distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. Together they form a grid of coordinates.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What do latitude and longitude tell us?
cards.answer: Latitude tells how far north or south a place is from the Equator; longitude tells how far east or west it is from the Prime Meridian.

chapters.title: Oceans and Continents
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Earth has large landmasses called continents and vast connected bodies of salt water called oceans. Land and water are distributed unevenly across the planet.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Use a world map to locate the seven continents and five oceans. Compare their relative positions and notice which continents are joined or separated by water.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Name the five oceans.
cards.answer: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic Oceans.

chapters.title: Landforms and Life
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Mountains, plateaus and plains are major landforms. Their height, slope, climate and resources influence where and how people live.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: People adapt homes, clothing, farming and transport to local landforms. Rivers, fertile soil and accessible routes can shape settlements.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How can a mountain environment influence people's way of life?
cards.answer: Steep slopes and colder conditions can affect farming, housing and travel; people adapt with suitable crops, homes and routes.

chapters.title: Timeline and Sources of History
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: History studies people and events of the past. Timelines arrange events in chronological order; sources such as objects, inscriptions, manuscripts and oral accounts provide evidence.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Ask who created a source, when and why. Archaeological sources include tools, pottery and buildings; literary sources include written texts.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why do historians use more than one type of source?
cards.answer: Different sources provide different clues and can support, question or add detail to one another, giving a fuller and more reliable picture of the past.

chapters.title: India, That Is Bharat
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: The names India and Bharat have long histories in texts and traditions. India's geography and its people have been connected through movement, exchange and shared cultural experiences.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Use maps and historical references carefully. Distinguish a name's historical use from the changing boundaries and political arrangements of different periods.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why is it useful to study both the names India and Bharat in history?
cards.answer: They appear in different historical sources and traditions, helping us understand how the land and its people have been described over time.

chapters.title: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: The Indus-Sarasvati or Harappan civilisation developed early urban settlements with planned streets, drainage, craft production and long-distance trade.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Study archaeological evidence such as seals, pottery, weights, buildings and town layouts. Do not assume that every feature of a civilisation is known from its script, which remains undeciphered.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Name two features that show planned urban life in Harappan cities.
cards.answer: Well-planned streets and drainage systems are two important examples; standardised weights and organised craft areas also provide evidence.

chapters.title: India’s Cultural Roots
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: India's cultural roots grew through many traditions, ideas, texts, teachers and practices. Philosophical questions, ethical teachings, art and ways of life shaped communities over time.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Notice both continuity and change. A tradition may be shared across regions while also developing local languages, customs and forms of expression.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does the phrase 'cultural roots' mean?
cards.answer: It refers to ideas, practices, stories, values and traditions from the past that continue to influence people's lives and culture.

chapters.title: Unity in Diversity, or ‘Many in the One’
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: India is home to many languages, foods, clothes, festivals, arts and customs. Diversity can coexist with shared experiences, values and a sense of belonging.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Look for examples of both difference and connection in daily life. Avoid assuming that everyone in a region follows exactly the same custom.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How can a country show unity while its people follow different languages and customs?
cards.answer: People can respect different ways of life while sharing common civic values, institutions, experiences and a sense of belonging.

chapters.title: Family and Community
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Families and communities are groups in which people care for one another, share responsibilities and cooperate. Their forms and roles can differ across places and time.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Notice the many kinds of work that support a community, including care work that may be unpaid or overlooked. Respect different family structures.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How does a community help people meet needs that one family may not meet alone?
cards.answer: People share knowledge, services, resources and support; cooperation helps the community solve common problems.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 1: Governance
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Governance is the way decisions are made and public services are organised. Democracy allows people to participate, choose representatives and hold decision-makers accountable.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Think about why decisions should be made close to the people affected by them. Participation, transparency and accountability strengthen local governance.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does accountability mean in a democracy?
cards.answer: People in authority must explain their decisions and can be questioned or held responsible for their actions.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Rural local government works through institutions such as the Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad. The Gram Sabha includes adult voters of a village or Gram Panchayat area.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: The Gram Sabha provides a forum for people to discuss local needs and question the Panchayat. Different levels coordinate village, block and district work.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Who are the members of a Gram Sabha?
cards.answer: All adult voters registered in the village or Gram Panchayat area are members of the Gram Sabha.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Urban local bodies manage services in towns and cities. Municipalities and Municipal Corporations work on issues such as water supply, roads, sanitation, street lighting and waste management.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: A city may be divided into wards represented by elected councillors. Citizens can raise local concerns through their ward representatives and civic bodies.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Name two services commonly managed by an urban local body.
cards.answer: Examples include waste collection, sanitation, local roads, street lighting and water supply.

chapters.title: The Value of Work
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: All kinds of work contribute to individuals, families and society. Work may be paid or unpaid, and care work is valuable even when it does not earn a wage.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Recognise the skills and effort involved in different occupations. Respect workers and avoid judging the worth of work only by its income.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why is unpaid care work valuable to society?
cards.answer: It supports people's health, learning and daily life, making it possible for families and communities to function.

chapters.title: Economic Activities Around Us
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Economic activities involve producing, distributing and consuming goods and services. People work in many occupations to meet needs and earn livelihoods.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Trace a product from its raw materials through production and transport to the person who uses it. Notice how producers, traders and consumers depend on one another.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the difference between a good and a service?
cards.answer: A good is a physical item that can be used, while a service is an activity or help provided to meet someone's need.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Rama Natha chases a magical potion instead of caring for his land. Sage Mahipati gives him a task that leads him to grow banana plants; Madhumati sells the fruit, and their steady work creates the wealth he wanted.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: The story contrasts a shortcut with patient effort. Notice how the sage guides Rama Natha through experience rather than simply arguing with him.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why does the sage ask Rama Natha to collect dew from banana leaves?
cards.answer: The task makes Rama Natha care for the plants over time. The real result is the banana harvest and the wealth earned through work, not a magic potion.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: A fox uses flattering words to make a raven show off its voice. When the raven opens its beak to sing, the food it holds falls and the fox gets it.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Identify the fox's intention, the raven's weakness and the consequence. The fable warns readers to think carefully before trusting praise.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What lesson does the raven learn from the fox's flattery?
cards.answer: Do not let praise make you careless or proud; think about a speaker's motive before believing flattering words.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: This humorous folk tale uses a misunderstanding around the name Rama and a timely arrival to help expose a thief. Quick thinking turns a confusing situation into a rescue.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Track who says or hears the name Rama and how the misunderstanding changes the events. Retell the sequence clearly rather than confusing the characters.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How does the misunderstanding about the name Rama help in the story?
cards.answer: It creates confusion for the thief and helps the real person named Rama arrive at the right moment, leading to the thief being caught.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Gajaraj, a royal elephant, feels lonely despite having every comfort. He and Buntee, a stray dog, become close friends; their separation makes both animals unhappy.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Notice how friendship grows through kindness and shared time, not wealth or status. The story also shows that animals can form strong bonds.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why are Gajaraj and Buntee called unlikely best friends?
cards.answer: They are very different animals and come from different circumstances, yet they form a deep friendship through companionship and care.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem expresses a wish to be a thoughtful friend: to give one's best, accept others without unfair judgement and genuinely wish them well.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Look for the speaker's promises and the values behind them. Explain how the poem describes friendship through actions and attitude.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What kind of friend does the speaker wish to be?
cards.answer: A caring, accepting and dependable friend who gives their best and does not judge others unfairly.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Mario's grandfather uses an imaginary chair to help him discover which classmates are genuine friends. Their reactions reveal who supports him and who enjoys seeing him struggle.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Distinguish real support from teasing or simply being present. The invisible-chair episode is a test of kindness and loyalty.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does the invisible-chair test help Mario understand?
cards.answer: It helps him recognise classmates who genuinely care and support him instead of laughing when he faces difficulty.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Amber speaks with a personified neem tree and learns about its names, history and many uses in everyday life, traditional care and the environment.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Personification gives the tree a voice. Separate the tree's real-life uses from the imaginative way the conversation is presented.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What literary device makes the neem tree speak to Amber?
cards.answer: Personification: the tree is given the human ability to speak and share its story.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem follows a young bird as its understanding of the world grows, moving from the shell to the nest, then to the wider world outside.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Notice how each new stage changes the bird's view. The poem uses a growing perspective to show discovery and learning.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How does the bird's idea of the world change as it grows?
cards.answer: Its world expands from the small space it first knows to the nest and then the wide world beyond.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: A grandmother's letter introduces familiar kitchen spices and describes how they are used in traditional home care, food and everyday wellness.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Recognise the spices and the uses described in the text, but distinguish traditional home practices from medical advice. Ask a trusted adult when unwell.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the main purpose of Daadi's letter about spices?
cards.answer: To share knowledge of common spices and their traditional uses, showing how food, culture and everyday care are connected.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Prabhat is obsessed with winning and even cheats during a game. Surya's cheerful attitude after losing helps Prabhat realise that enjoying the game and playing fairly matter more than winning.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Compare Prabhat's attitude before and after meeting Surya. Look for the moment that changes his understanding of sportsmanship.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What causes Prabhat's change of heart?
cards.answer: Surya enjoys playing even after losing, which makes Prabhat realise that fair play, effort and enjoyment matter more than the result.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem describes children playing until the day ends. Personification gives the natural end of the game a playful sense of victory.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Notice the poem's images of play, evening and tiredness. Explain how personification makes the ending memorable.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Who is described as the winner at the end of the poem, and why?
cards.answer: Night is playfully presented as the winner because darkness ends the children's game.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The text presents yoga as a practice that connects body and mind. It describes yoga's Indian roots and its role in physical fitness, calmness and well-being.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Remember that yoga includes more than physical postures; breathing, attention and balanced habits are also important.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does the word yoga suggest in the text?
cards.answer: It comes from a Sanskrit root meaning to join or unite, expressing harmony between body and mind and between thought and action.

cards.title: Story / poem idea

cards.title: Notice and explain

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How can India's diversity be seen in everyday life?
cards.answer: Through its many languages, foods, clothing styles, art forms, festivals, landscapes and regional traditions.

chapters.title: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with her Feet

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Ila Sachani, from Gujarat, develops great skill in Kathiawar embroidery by learning to use her feet because she cannot use her hands in the usual way. Her family encourages her talent.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Focus on the support she receives, the skill she develops and how determination opens opportunities. Do not reduce her story to disability alone; recognise her artistry.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How did Ila Sachani learn to create embroidery despite the challenge she faced?
cards.answer: With encouragement from her mother and grandmother, she practised and developed the skill of using her feet to create intricate embroidery.

cards.question: Why is a National War Memorial important?
cards.answer: It honours and remembers soldiers' service and sacrifice, helping citizens express gratitude and reflect on peace and responsibility.

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में मातृभूमि के प्रति प्रेम, सम्मान और कृतज्ञता का भाव व्यक्त होता है। देश की प्रकृति, संस्कृति और लोगों से जुड़ाव कविता का मुख्य आधार है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कविता पढ़ते समय देश के प्रति भाव, चित्रात्मक शब्दों और कवि के संदेश को पहचानें। अपने शब्दों में बताएं कि मातृभूमि हमारे लिए क्यों महत्त्वपूर्ण है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: ‘मातृभूमि’ कविता का मुख्य भाव क्या है?
cards.answer: मातृभूमि के प्रति प्रेम, सम्मान और उसके प्रति अपने कर्तव्यों का बोध।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: ‘गोल’ संस्मरण में हॉकी के अनुभवों के माध्यम से खेल के प्रति लगन, अभ्यास, अनुशासन और टीम भावना का महत्त्व उभरता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: घटना-क्रम याद रखें और समझें कि सफलता केवल व्यक्तिगत कौशल से नहीं, बल्कि अभ्यास और साथियों के सहयोग से भी मिलती है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: खेल में टीम भावना क्यों आवश्यक है?
cards.answer: टीम भावना से खिलाड़ी एक-दूसरे का सहयोग करते हैं, मिलकर रणनीति बनाते हैं और सामूहिक लक्ष्य प्राप्त करते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में वर्षा की पहली बूँद से प्रकृति में आने वाली ताजगी और जीवन की नई उमंग का चित्रण है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कविता के प्रकृति-चित्रों और ध्वनि/दृश्य बिंबों पर ध्यान दें। बताएं कि पहली वर्षा धरती और मन को कैसे प्रभावित करती है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: पहली बूँद के आने से प्रकृति में क्या परिवर्तन दिखाई देता है?
cards.answer: धरती में ताजगी आती है, मिट्टी की सुगंध फैलती है और पेड़-पौधे तथा जीव-जगत प्रसन्न और सक्रिय हो उठते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कहानी में बाबा भारती का घोड़ा सुल्तान और खड़गसिंह की घटना के माध्यम से दया, विश्वास और मानवीयता का संदेश मिलता है। बाबा भारती घोड़े से अधिक मनुष्य के भीतर की अच्छाई को महत्त्व देते हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: बाबा भारती और खड़गसिंह के व्यवहार में आए परिवर्तन की तुलना करें। कहानी का शीर्षक बाहरी हार के बजाय नैतिक विजय की ओर संकेत करता है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: कहानी में ‘हार की जीत’ किस अर्थ में है?
cards.answer: बाबा भारती का विश्वास और करुणा अंततः खड़गसिंह के मन को बदल देते हैं। नैतिकता और मानवता की जीत होती है।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: रहीम के दोहों में विनम्रता, प्रेम, संबंधों की मर्यादा, परोपकार और व्यवहार-कुशलता जैसे जीवन-मूल्य सरल उदाहरणों से समझाए गए हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: हर दोहे का सरल अर्थ लिखें और उससे मिलने वाली सीख को अपने जीवन के उदाहरण से जोड़ें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: रहीम के दोहे हमें किस प्रकार का व्यवहार अपनाने की सीख देते हैं?
cards.answer: विनम्र, संवेदनशील और परोपकारी व्यवहार; संबंधों का सम्मान और दूसरों की भावनाओं का ध्यान।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: इस आत्मकथात्मक पाठ में माँ के स्नेह, त्याग, साहस और संस्कारों का प्रभाव सामने आता है। माँ का मार्गदर्शन व्यक्ति के चरित्र और जीवन-मूल्यों को आकार देता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: लेखक की माँ के गुणों को पाठ के प्रसंगों से समझाएँ। केवल विशेषण लिखने के बजाय बताएं कि उनके व्यवहार से कौन-सा गुण प्रकट होता है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: लेखक के जीवन पर माँ का क्या प्रभाव पड़ा?
cards.answer: माँ के स्नेह, साहस और संस्कारों ने लेखक को प्रेरित किया तथा उसके व्यक्तित्व और जीवन-मूल्यों को मजबूत बनाया।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में दीप जलाने का प्रतीक आशा, ज्ञान, साहस और निरंतर अच्छे कार्य करते रहने का संदेश देता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: दीपक को केवल वस्तु न मानें; कविता में उसका प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ समझें। बताएं कि कठिन समय में आशा बनाए रखना क्यों जरूरी है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: कविता में दीप जलाने का प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ क्या है?
cards.answer: अंधकार और निराशा को दूर करके आशा, ज्ञान और सकारात्मकता फैलाते रहना।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: पाठ में असम की दो विशिष्ट नृत्य परंपराओं—सत्रिया और बिहू—का परिचय मिलता है। ये राज्य की सांस्कृतिक पहचान, इतिहास और सामुदायिक जीवन से जुड़ी हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: सत्रिया और बिहू की उत्पत्ति, अवसर, वेशभूषा और प्रस्तुति के अंतर को अलग-अलग बिंदुओं में लिखें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: सत्रिया और बिहू नृत्य में एक प्रमुख अंतर बताइए।
cards.answer: सत्रिया असम की शास्त्रीय नृत्य परंपरा है, जबकि बिहू असम के लोकजीवन और बिहू उत्सवों से जुड़ा लोकनृत्य है।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: सूरदास के पद में बालकृष्ण की चंचलता और माँ यशोदा के साथ उनका नटखट संवाद दिखाई देता है। कृष्ण माखन खाने से इनकार करते हुए भोलेपन से अपनी बात रखते हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कृष्ण की बाल-लीलाओं, संवाद की चंचलता और वात्सल्य रस को पहचानें। पद की भाषा में लोक-जीवन की सहजता भी दिखाई देती है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: कृष्ण यशोदा से क्या कहते हैं?
cards.answer: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि उन्होंने माखन नहीं खाया और अपनी मासूमियत भरे तर्कों से माँ को समझाने का प्रयास करते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: देवगढ़ रियासत के लिए नया दीवान चुनना है। सरदार सुजानसिंह उम्मीदवारों की केवल डिग्री नहीं, बल्कि उनके आचरण, दया, साहस और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा को परखते हैं। पंडित जानकीनाथ घायल होने पर भी एक गरीब किसान की गाड़ी दलदल से निकालने में मदद करते हैं और इसी मानवीय व्यवहार के कारण चुने जाते हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कहानी में उम्मीदवारों के दिखावटी शिष्टाचार और जानकीनाथ के वास्तविक सेवाभाव का अंतर समझें। दीवान चुनने की कसौटी—दया, उदारता, आत्मबल और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा—घटनाओं से स्पष्ट करें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: पंडित जानकीनाथ को देवगढ़ का दीवान क्यों चुना गया?
cards.answer: उन्होंने स्वयं घायल होने के बावजूद एक गरीब किसान की अनाज से भरी गाड़ी को दलदल से निकालने में मदद की। उनके व्यवहार से दया, साहस, उदारता और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा प्रकट हुई।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में महाराणा प्रताप के घोड़े चेतक की निष्ठा, साहस और स्वामीभक्ति का वर्णन है। संकट की घड़ी में चेतक का धैर्य और बलिदान वीरता का उदाहरण बनता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कविता में चेतक के गुणों को घटनाओं से जोड़ें। वीरता के साथ निष्ठा और त्याग के भाव को भी समझें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: चेतक को वीर और निष्ठावान क्यों कहा गया है?
cards.answer: उसने संकट में महाराणा प्रताप का साथ नहीं छोड़ा और अपनी शक्ति तथा साहस से उन्हें सुरक्षित पहुँचाने में योगदान दिया।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: यात्रा-वृत्तांत में हिंद महासागर के एक द्वीप-समाज में भारतीय मूल के लोगों, भाषा, संस्कृति और परंपराओं की झलक मिलती है। प्रवास के बाद भी सांस्कृतिक संबंध कैसे बने रहते हैं, यह पाठ दिखाता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: यात्रा-वृत्तांत में स्थान, लोगों, रीति-रिवाजों और लेखक के अनुभवों को पहचानें। भारत से दूर रहते हुए भी संस्कृति के बने रहने के उदाहरण खोजें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: ‘छोटा-सा हिंदुस्तान’ किस अर्थ में कहा गया है?
cards.answer: विदेश में बसे भारतीय मूल के लोगों ने अपनी भाषा, परंपराओं, त्योहारों और सांस्कृतिक पहचान को सँजोकर रखा है; इसलिए वहाँ भारत की झलक दिखाई देती है।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: पाठ पेड़ों के जीवन, प्रकृति में उनके योगदान और मनुष्य के साथ उनके संबंध पर ध्यान दिलाता है। पेड़ पर्यावरण, भोजन, छाया, हवा और अनेक जीवों के आश्रय के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: पेड़ों के लाभों को पर्यावरण, जीव-जगत और मानव जीवन के संदर्भ में अलग-अलग समझें। संरक्षण के व्यावहारिक उपाय भी सोचें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: पेड़ प्रकृति और मनुष्य के लिए क्यों आवश्यक हैं?
cards.answer: पेड़ हवा को शुद्ध करने, छाया और भोजन देने, मिट्टी बचाने, जलचक्र में मदद करने और अनेक जीवों को आश्रय देने में महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।
